title: Winning the Down Beat poll
summary: McGhee wonders at his award, linking it to Granz, and notes leaders could not be voted for.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, that was the year I won the Downbeat Award, and they knew about it -- how they knew, I don't know.
Oh, they knew all those things.
Yeah, they knew all about it. I didn't even know about it myself! They told me, 'Yeah, you were first this year.' I said, 'Oh yeah? I didn't know nothin' about that.' They said, 'Well, yeah, we do.'

Delaunay, you know, this guy that I was telling you about, I didn't have the slightest idea that that's what would be happening... But I think it was on account of Norman Granz, he had pulled a lot of strings or something. Because I mean, I think that they should have given it to Dizzy first...
Well, in those days in the Downbeat Poll you weren't allowed to vote for a leader.
Oh yeah, that's right. I guess that's why Diz didn't get it first.
Then they changed it, I think.
Yeah. Because I saw Dizzy down at Birdland
when they were giving me my plaque, and he told me, "Gee, I sure wish I could get one of them." I said, "Well, you'll get yours, don't worry." I'm sure he got them all over the place now.
Well, I remember Miles, he always used to put them down, and then when I went to his apartment, he had them all over the wall!
Yeah! Heh-heh, that's where they go. Let's see, I think Miles came on the scene... He started getting into it in '47 -- or '48, I guess it was. He came in third, fourth, third, second, then first.
